PTP - here goes a dumb question...

What are you referring to when you use the term 'rotation'? Do you mean price returning to an important zone and reacting?

Also, and perhaps an equally dumb question: is how do you read tick charts? I have never gone lower than a 1- minute chart. When I do, it looks like this (50 T)

Rotation = is price rolling over in supply or demand.

Tick Charts - every tick represents a trade and is accumulated into a bucket - the candle. So if you have a 100 tick chart, that candle represents 100 trades....at least for futures. Non-time based charts can be helpful at times, and not so helpful at others -another art to be mastered.

Thanks PTP

I have two main questions to research and study:

1. Are HTF QM setups more reliable than LTF QM setups? From what I have seen, the 1 Min and 5 Min charts are unpredictable when it comes to the QM PA. They fail frequently. QM's that form on the HTF charts seem to have better follow through.

2. Is there a way to predict a diamond formation? My understanding from the Marketpedia section is a diamond is essentially a failed QM with an additional HH or LL that eclipses the previous HH or LL. Is a diamond formation a fakeout of the failed QM's original HH/LL? If so, is there a way to predict this diamond or do we always have to account for the possibility that one may form? If we must always account for the possibility of a diamond, doesn't that significantly add to the risk of a trade?

I will do some more research and look through some of the Masters journals to see if these questions can be answered.
